reasons: The rule's detection guidance treats the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months as a missing-behaviour deviation; the cited Section 9 paragraphs (for-cause/security-based Order Form termination in 9.3, survival/severability of termination rights in 9.5) contain no no-fault exit, and the consecutive paragraph IDs (p0040 → p0041) corroborate that no 9.4 clause sits between 9.3 and 9.5.

Redline reaches the preferred position with a single targeted insertion: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, express no early-termination penalty, and no Vendor mid-term convenience right — matching the model language and using defined terms (Agreement, Order Form, Fees, Vendor) correctly.

Nothing in the existing clauses is deleted or degraded, so this is the smallest edit that achieves the playbook position; the added Vendor-side sentence merely confirms the status quo and does not disadvantage us.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, cites the three-year term and the playbook rationale, and offers the 60-day fallback.

Only minor nits, not grounds for failure: the inserted sentence is appended to p0040 without its own '9.4' numbering, and it does not restate the fee-cap fallback in the text (the fallback is offered in the comment instead).
